extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of English poetry and literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and critical principles for assessing English poets (especially Burns, Wordsworth) and old ballads — focusing on tone, imagery, social content, musicality, and the character of genius and fame. Drawn from a lecture-style literary-criticism treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic spirit: sentiment vs. animal existence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mr. Wordsworth's poetry is the poetry of mere sentiment and pensive contemplation: Burns's is a very highly sublimated essence of animal existence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a poem's spirit is inward, contemplative and 'sentimental' (Wordsworthian) or whether it embodies vigorous social/physical life ('animal existence') as Burns does. Anti-pattern: poetry that is aloof from lived bodily/social experience when the subject demands vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness and gaiety
rubrics_metrics.description: "He is 'famous for the keeping of it up,' and in his verse is ever fresh and gay."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value continual vivacity and a sense of being 'ever fresh and gay' in verse. Examples: Burns's convivial songs. Anti-pattern: passages that feel tedious or worn-out; criticisms that prize solemnity at the expense of liveliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of bodily and social life
rubrics_metrics.description: "From the Lyrical Ballads, it does not appear that men eat or drink, marry or are given in marriage." (contrast praising Burns's exaltation of wine, love, and good fellowship)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether poetry engages with daily bodily and social practices (eating, drinking, marriage, fellowship). Burns is praised for exalting these; omission can be a failing if the poem's aim is to portray full human life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid local description and comic painting
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: "The 'Halloween' is the most striking and picturesque description of local customs and scenery... Brigs of Ayr, Address to a Haggis, Scotch Drink... full of characteristic and comic painting."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward precise local colour, picturesque scene-setting, and comic/characterful portraiture. Use concrete local customs and dialect to create vividness (e.g., Tam o' Shanter). Anti-pattern: generic or abstract descriptions lacking particularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solemn pathos and devotional feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Cotter's Saturday Night is a noble and pathetic picture of human manners, mingled with a fine religious awe."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the combination of domestic realism and genuine devotional emotion; the ability to evoke slow, solemn music-like pathos. Example: the stanzas quoted from 'The Cotter's Saturday Night.' Anti-pattern: forced sentiment or didactic moralising that lacks genuine feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic imagery and intimacy with nature (ballads)
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is in them a still more original cast of thought, a more romantic imagery — ... a closer intimacy with nature."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for original, romantic images drawn closely from natural detail (thistle's glittering down, hawk on its perch, horseman's silver bells). Ballads are praised when they show intimate, unforced reliance on nature as a source of imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of manners and strength of affection
rubrics_metrics.description: "A more infantine simplicity of manners, a greater strength of affection, hopes longer cherished and longer deferred..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward plain, direct manners and powerful, enduring feelings rather than ornate sophistication. Anti-pattern: overwrought or artificially complex social manners in a ballad context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistolary poetry: satire, character-painting, and sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Burns's poetical epistles to his friends are admirable, whether for the touches of satire, the painting of character, or the sincerity of friendship they display."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good poetic letters combine sharp satirical touches, clear portraiture of character, and authentic friendship/sincerity. Use these axes to judge strengths of epistolary poems; weak examples may be insincere or merely clever without heart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose letters: avoid affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: "His prose-letters are sometimes tinctured with affectation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In prose correspondence, naturalness and candid expression are virtues; affectation diminishes trustworthiness and artistic worth. Revise for a more straightforward voice when prose feels posed or performance-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skillful imitation of traditional forms
rubrics_metrics.description: "His imitations of the old humorous ballad style of Ferguson's songs are no whit inferior to the admirable originals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how well a modern poem reproduces the qualities of older forms (tone, diction, rhythm, humour). Successful imitation should stand alongside originals rather than feeling like pastiche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathos and seriousness in love-songs
rubrics_metrics.description: "Of all his productions, the pathetic and serious love-songs which he has left behind him, in the manner of the old ballads, are perhaps those which take the deepest and most lasting hold of the mind."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge love-songs by their ability to reach deep emotional resonance and lasting impact through seriousness and genuine pathos. Light flirtation or prettiness is less prized than heartfelt, ballad-style sorrow or longing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballad energy: liveliness, adventure, and convivial subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: "The old English ballads are of a gayer and more lively turn. They are adventurous and romantic; but they relate chiefly to good living and good fellowship, to drinking and hunting scenes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ballads, value brisk action, adventurous plots, and celebration of fellowship and good living. Expect scenes of feasting, hunting, revelry, and clear narrative movement. Anti-pattern: stillness and excessive interiority in a ballad meant to be rollicking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary love of nature over self-admiration (character of genius)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The love of nature is the first thing in the mind of the true poet: the admiration of himself the last."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a poet's motives: genuine poets foreground nature and truth; self-admiration or vanity signals lesser artistic stature. Works that seem exercises in self-display are judged less favorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience for posterity; avoid seeking immediate fame
rubrics_metrics.description: "Fame is the recompense not of the living, but of the dead... He who would be great in the eyes of others, must first learn to be nothing in his own."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure a poet's artistic maturity by willingness to wait for long-term judgment rather than chasing ephemeral publicity. Anti-pattern: 'mortgaging' immortality for a newspaper puff or courting instant applause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on subject rather than audience or self
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do you suppose that Shakspeare... was thinking of any thing but Lear and Othello?... he who would be great... must first learn to be nothing in his own."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good creative work concentrates on the integrity of the subject/characters rather than tailoring itself to please an audience or to self-promote. Anti-pattern: writing primarily to flatter or to manufacture reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple musicality in domestic and religious song
rubrics_metrics.description: "They chant their artless notes in simple guise; They tune their hearts, by far the noblest aim... Compar'd with these, Italian trills are tame; The tickled ears no heart-felt raptures raise; Nae unison hae they with our Creator's praise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value plain, artless musical expression in domestic or devotional songs over ornate virtuosity. Simplicity that moves the heart is preferable to technical showmanship in contexts of communal or religious singing.
